investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) Across All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval environment has hit the maximum allowed concurrent swarm agents, preventing the observability check from provisioning a new agent and satisfying the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 concurrent agents per org (or globally per environment). At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T15:45:36Z), that limit was already at capacity, causing POST /api/agents to return 409 Conflict with code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval check depends on successfully creating a new agent to collect vmIdPresent and remoteState evidence, the entire check pipeline fails before any VM is provisioned. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence in the supplied data indicates a broader production outage beyond the inability to create additional agents.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} at 2026-06-14T15:45:36.096Z

All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure is at the agent-creation step shared by all checks — not in VM readiness or runtime polling.

The inner swarm error code is 'conflict' with message 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', indicating the swarm layer itself is enforcing the cap and rejecting the request before any VM is allocated.
Evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are all absent from the check evidence object, consistent with the request being rejected before any agent resource was created.
Latency for all three failing checks is low (985–1510 ms), well under the warning threshold of 30000 ms, confirming the failure is an immediate rejection, not a timeout or slow provisioning issue.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval environment's swarm org has accumulated 100 live agents from previous eval runs that were not cleaned up (e.g., prior check runs that created agents but whose teardown/delete step failed or was never implemented), exhausting the quota.
[Likely] A separate production or staging workload sharing the same swarm org or quota namespace has consumed all 100 agent slots, leaving none available for the eval check.
[Possible] The quota limit of 100 is a global swarm-level cap (not per-org) and concurrent load from multiple environments or tenants has collectively reached it.

[Less likely] The eval check is incorrectly reusing an agent identity that already exists (the outer error says 'swarm agent already exists'), suggesting the check may be attempting to create an agent with a deterministic/fixed name that was never deleted from a prior run, triggering both a 'already exists' and a 'quota exceeded' condition simultaneously from the swarm layer.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Checks Failing with 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100)
investigation.summary: All three Remote Agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T15:45 with identical 409 Conflict responses from POST /api/agents, indicating the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation because the agent quota of 100 has been reached for the eval's target organization or environment. No state polling evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected because agent creation is a prerequisite that never succeeded.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call made by the eval harness. Because agent creation is the first step in the Remote Agents check pipeline, all downstream checks (state polling, runtime readiness) also failed — not due to independent faults, but because they depend on a successfully created agent. The quota ceiling of 100 agents has been reached in the target swarm environment used by the eval, blocking any new agent provisioning.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three sibling checks: remote-agent-create (endedAt 2026-06-14T15:45:37.606Z, latency 1510ms), remote-agent-state (endedAt 2026-06-14T15:45:38.617Z, latency 1011ms), remote-agent-runtime (endedAt 2026-06-14T15:45:39.602Z, latency 985ms).

Error payload is identical across all three checks: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm layer enforces a hard cap of 100 agents.
All three checks have empty evidence objects ({}) — no orgId, agentId, readyState, or state was captured — consistent with failure at the creation step before any state could be observed.

Latencies for all three calls (985ms–1510ms) are well below the warningLatencyMs threshold of 5000ms, ruling out a timeout or latency-related failure; the rejection was immediate from the swarm backend.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval harness's dedicated swarm environment or org account has accumulated 100 agents from prior eval runs and the cleanup/teardown step is not deleting them, causing the quota to fill up over time.
[Likely] A previous eval run crashed or was interrupted before its teardown phase, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota without being reclaimed.

[Possible] The eval harness is creating agents in a shared swarm environment (e.g., production org) rather than an isolated eval-specific org/namespace, causing eval agents to compete with real agents for quota.
[Less likely] The swarm backend's quota limit of 100 is too low for the combined load of concurrent eval runs plus any real agents, and the limit itself needs to be raised for the eval environment.
[Unlikely] A swarm-side bug is miscounting active agents and reporting quota exceeded prematurely before the true limit is reached.

reproductionSteps.details: If the response returns 100 agents, quota exhaustion is confirmed.

reproductionSteps.details: Inspect the agent list for agents with eval-harness naming patterns or creation timestamps predating the current run. These are candidates for stale/orphaned agents that were not cleaned up.

reproductionSteps.details: Issue DELETE /api/agents/{agentId} for each orphaned eval agent to free quota slots, then re-run the eval to confirm it passes.

reproductionSteps.details: Trigger the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks again. All three should pass if quota was the sole blocker.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect eval harness teardown logic for agent deletion
reproductionSteps.details: Review the eval harness setup/teardown lifecycle to confirm a DELETE call is issued for every agent created during a run, including on error paths and interrupted runs.

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (409 Conflict) Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T15:45 with identical 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval cannot provision a new agent to run its test lifecycle, so no expected output contract assertions (e.g., "hello from aura" message) can be evaluated.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is returning a hard quota error — "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" — on POST /api/agents. The eval harness attempts to create a fresh agent at the start of each check run, but the quota ceiling is already at capacity, causing every creation attempt to fail with HTTP 409 before any agent lifecycle or chat-readiness assertions can be reached. This is an eval infrastructure / environment resource exhaustion issue, not a runtime logic or latency failure.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned HTTP 409 with the identical error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The error message explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm backend has a hard cap of 100 agents and that cap is currently met.

Latency for all three failing calls was well under the warning threshold (985 ms, 1510 ms, 1011 ms vs. 20000 ms warning / 60000 ms outage thresholds), confirming the service itself is responsive — the failure is a business-logic quota rejection, not a latency or availability outage.

The failure cascade is sequential and consistent: remote-agent-create failed first (endedAt 15:45:37.606Z), then remote-agent-state (15:45:38.617Z), then remote-agent-runtime (15:45:39.602Z), matching the expected eval execution order and confirming all downstream checks fail as a direct consequence of the creation failure.
No evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals was supplied; this failure is scoped to the AURA eval environment.
possibleCauses: (Highest confidence) The eval environment's swarm org or account has accumulated 100 agents from previous eval runs that were not cleaned up, exhausting the quota and preventing new agent creation.
(High confidence) The eval harness does not perform teardown/cleanup of agents it creates, causing quota to grow monotonically across runs until the hard limit is hit.
(Medium confidence) A prior eval run crashed or was interrupted before its cleanup step, leaving one or more orphaned agents that consumed the remaining quota slots.

(Lower confidence) The quota limit of 100 is shared between the eval environment and other workloads (e.g., staging or developer testing) on the same org/account, and external activity consumed the remaining capacity.

(Lower confidence) The swarm backend's conflict detection is incorrectly identifying a new agent creation as a duplicate ('swarm agent already exists') due to a naming or ID collision in the eval harness, triggering the quota error path prematurely.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame and never producing the required `generation_completed` frame or an artifact URL. The stream terminated in 1933 ms with no progress frames, confirming the harness was unreachable at eval time.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness returned HTTP 404 when the eval harness attempted to open a session for image generation. This means the target endpoint resolved by `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` or `SWARM_BASE_URL` either does not exist at the configured address, is running an incompatible (mismatched route) version, or was not deployed/running at the time of the eval. The failure is localized to the session-open handshake of the image generation stream route — no generation work was attempted and no frames beyond `generation_start` and `generation_error` were emitted.
proof: The `generation_error` frame carries code `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` and message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
The stream produced only two meaningful frames — `generation_start` and `generation_error` — and a trailing empty `message` frame, confirming the session never progressed past the open handshake.
Required evidence keys `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent` are both missing from the collected evidence, consistent with the stream aborting before any generation frames were emitted.
Eval latency was 1933 ms, well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms, indicating a fast-fail network/routing error rather than a timeout or slow generation path.
The `generation_start` frame was emitted with `mode: image`, confirming the eval harness reached the stream entry point but the downstream agent runtime session-open call failed immediately.
possibleCauses: (Most likely) The agent runtime harness is not deployed or not running at the address configured in `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL`, causing every session-open request to receive a 404.

(Likely) The harness is deployed but at an incompatible version whose session-open route path has changed (e.g., route renamed or versioned), so the configured URL resolves to a valid host but a non-existent endpoint path.

(Possible) The environment variable `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` or `SWARM_BASE_URL` is misconfigured (wrong host, port, or base path) in the production eval environment, pointing to a host that returns 404 for the session-open route.
(Less likely) A recent deployment rolled back or removed the agent runtime service in the production environment, leaving the URL configured but the service absent.
(Less likely) A network-layer proxy or ingress rule is intercepting the request and returning 404 before it reaches the harness process.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame and never producing the required `generation_completed` frame or an artifact URL. The stream terminated in 1933 ms with no progress frames, confirming the harness was unreachable at eval time.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness returned HTTP 404 when the eval harness attempted to open a session for image generation. This means the target endpoint resolved by `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` or `SWARM_BASE_URL` either does not exist at the configured address, is running an incompatible (mismatched route) version, or was not deployed/running at the time of the eval. The failure is localized to the session-open handshake of the image generation stream route — no generation work was attempted and no frames beyond `generation_start` and `generation_error` were emitted.
proof: The `generation_error` frame carries code `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` and message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
The stream produced only two meaningful frames — `generation_start` and `generation_error` — and a trailing empty `message` frame, confirming the session never progressed past the open handshake.
Required evidence keys `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent` are both missing from the collected evidence, consistent with the stream aborting before any generation frames were emitted.
Eval latency was 1933 ms, well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms, indicating a fast-fail network/routing error rather than a timeout or slow generation path.
The `generation_start` frame was emitted with `mode: image`, confirming the eval harness reached the stream entry point but the downstream agent runtime session-open call failed immediately.
possibleCauses: (Most likely) The agent runtime harness is not deployed or not running at the address configured in `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL`, causing every session-open request to receive a 404.

(Likely) The harness is deployed but at an incompatible version whose session-open route path has changed (e.g., route renamed or versioned), so the configured URL resolves to a valid host but a non-existent endpoint path.

(Possible) The environment variable `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` or `SWARM_BASE_URL` is misconfigured (wrong host, port, or base path) in the production eval environment, pointing to a host that returns 404 for the session-open route.
(Less likely) A recent deployment rolled back or removed the agent runtime service in the production environment, leaving the URL configured but the service absent.
(Less likely) A network-layer proxy or ingress rule is intercepting the request and returning 404 before it reaches the harness process.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) Across All Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval environment has hit the maximum allowed concurrent swarm agents, preventing the observability check from provisioning a new agent and satisfying the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 concurrent agents per org (or globally per environment). At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T15:45:36Z), that limit was already at capacity, causing POST /api/agents to return 409 Conflict with code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval check depends on successfully creating a new agent to collect vmIdPresent and remoteState evidence, the entire check pipeline fails before any VM is provisioned. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence in the supplied data indicates a broader production outage beyond the inability to create additional agents.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} at 2026-06-14T15:45:36.096Z

All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure is at the agent-creation step shared by all checks — not in VM readiness or runtime polling.

The inner swarm error code is 'conflict' with message 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', indicating the swarm layer itself is enforcing the cap and rejecting the request before any VM is allocated.
Evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are all absent from the check evidence object, consistent with the request being rejected before any agent resource was created.
Latency for all three failing checks is low (985–1510 ms), well under the warning threshold of 30000 ms, confirming the failure is an immediate rejection, not a timeout or slow provisioning issue.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval environment's swarm org has accumulated 100 live agents from previous eval runs that were not cleaned up (e.g., prior check runs that created agents but whose teardown/delete step failed or was never implemented), exhausting the quota.
[Likely] A separate production or staging workload sharing the same swarm org or quota namespace has consumed all 100 agent slots, leaving none available for the eval check.
[Possible] The quota limit of 100 is a global swarm-level cap (not per-org) and concurrent load from multiple environments or tenants has collectively reached it.

[Less likely] The eval check is incorrectly reusing an agent identity that already exists (the outer error says 'swarm agent already exists'), suggesting the check may be attempting to create an agent with a deterministic/fixed name that was never deleted from a prior run, triggering both a 'already exists' and a 'quota exceeded' condition simultaneously from the swarm layer.

Eval: orphaned agent detection — periodically list all agents in the eval org and assert that no agents older than (staleAfterMinutes * 2 = 40 minutes) with eval harness naming conventions exist.

Eval: quota error disambiguation — assert that a 409 response from POST /api/agents with code 'conflict' is further classified as either 'duplicate_agent' or 'quota_exceeded' to distinguish infrastructure exhaustion from logic errors.
Eval: isolated agent creation smoke test — run a minimal agent creation + deletion round-trip in a quota-isolated test org to confirm the swarm creation path is healthy independent of quota state.
